paragraphs: R. Chiyya bar Abba, the priest.

(a) An outstanding student of R. Yochanan. He came up from Babylonia, and R. Yochanan called him “Babylonian”; see above. He reviewed his learning before R. Yochanan every thirty days: Chullin 86b; Berakhot 38b. Tosafot writes that this does not literally mean all his learning: whatever he learned in thirty days, he reviewed on the thirty-first. Beer Sheva, on Keritot, writes that this explanation is impossible, since then Keritot 27a, near the end, would raise no objection. Rather, it means all his learning; similarly Rav Sheshet, see there. There is compelling evidence from Rav Ashi and R. Chanina bar Pappa. The statement there in Keritot that “R. Zeira bar Adda reviewed his learning” is a scribal error and should read “R. Chiyya bar Abba.” End of quotation. See Rav Yehudah, who prayed only on the thirtieth day, because he reviewed his learning every thirty days. Yuchasin writes in connection with the Epistle of Rav Sherira Gaon, “He leaned against the door bolt and said, ‘Rejoice, my soul: for you I read.’” This is a scribal error, for Rav Sheshet did this; see there, Pesachim 68b.

(b) “He died before R. Yochanan.” I do not know whence this is derived. If it is because Berakhot 5b says that R. Chiyya bar Abba fell ill and R. Yochanan visited him and asked, “Are sufferings dear to you?” He answered, “Neither they nor their reward,” etc., and R. Yochanan gave him his hand and raised him—then it explicitly says that R. Yochanan raised him! But the Jerusalem Talmud apparently places him after R. Yehudah Nesia. The intended reference is Jerusalem Berakhot, chapter 3, mishnah 1: when R. Yehudah Nesia, Rabbi's grandson, died, R. Chiyya bar Abba pushed R. Zeira and made him impure. All the more so, then, after R. Yochanan—that is, R. Yochanan died before R. Yehudah Nesia. Apparently they learned that R. Yochanan died before R. Yehudah Nesia from Rosh Hashanah 20a: R. Yehudah Nesia sent to R. Ammi, “Throughout R. Yochanan's life he taught us, etc.” This supposedly proves that R. Yochanan died before R. Yehudah Nesia. But it does not: Tosafot writes that this R. Yehudah Nesia, R. Yochanan's student, was the grandson of the R. Yehudah Nesia who was Rabbi's grandson; see there.

(c) Jerusalem Maaser Sheni, chapter 5, halakhah 5: R. Chiyya bar Ba ruled for himself to leave the Land so as not to receive tithe. In Jerusalem Berakhot, chapter 3, mishnah 1, he stepped over graves to see King Diocletian, since a priest may become impure to see a king. He went out in patched shoes: Berakhot 43b. Ketubot 8b: R. Chiyya bar Abba taught Scripture or Mishnah to R. Yehoshua ben Levi's son, and brought Yehudah bar Nachmani, his interpreter. Were I not afraid, I would say this is a scribal error and should read “Rav Chiyya bar Adda” (see there), who taught Resh Lakish's young children. Hence the reading in the Gemara and Ein Yaakov is “Rav Chiyya bar Abba taught Scripture, etc.” If this were Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba, he is called Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba throughout the Talmud. Furthermore, if R. Chiyya bar Abba taught Scripture or Mishnah to R. Yehoshua ben Levi's son, why do you not find him saying anything in Resh Lakish's name anywhere in the Talmud? This requires investigation.

(d) R. Abba, in his name—Rabbah, portion Behar, section 33. Megillah 30a: “R. Chiyya bar Abba said: R. Abba said.” “R. Abba said: R. Chiyya bar Abba said”—Shabbat 113a; this should be the reading, and so it is in Rif. R. Abba, his son. R. Abba bar Mammal objected to him. R. Abba bar Shmuel asked him. R. Abbahu expounded aggadot while he expounded legal teachings; see there. R. Avin, in his name. Rav Acha, his son—this requires investigation. Aivu bar Nagri, in his name. R. Aleksandri, in his name. And R. Ilai. R. Ammi said to him, “Let the Master say”—Zevachim 85b; Chullin 103a; Bava Kamma 20b. He spoke in R. Yochanan's name, and R. Ammi and R. Assi turned away their faces, meaning that R. Yochanan had not said it: Yoma 73a. He sat with R. Assi before R. Yochanan, who called them “children”: Shabbat 145b; also before R. Yochanan in Eruvin 65b, near the end. R. Assi disagrees with him at the end of Mi SheHafakh. He was present at R. Assi's death. Rav Ashi told him three things in R. Yehoshua ben Levi's name. Balu, in his name. And Rav Bivi. R. Banai, his brother. Binyamin bar Ashtor. And R. Binyamin bar Yefet. R. Berekhiah, in his name. R. Hillel bar Vallas, in his name. “Rav Huna said: R. Chiyya bar Abba said: R. Yochanan said”—Moed Katan 20a. R. Zeira said: “Hold fast to R. Chiyya bar Abba's version, because he is precise and learns a teaching well from its master's mouth”: Berakhot 33b, 38b; Sukkah 45. “R. Chiyya [bar Abba] said: R. Yochanan said, etc.” R. Zeira said to R. Chiyya bar Abba, “But perhaps, etc.” He answered, “Hasty fool!”: Zevachim 25b. He prayed and then prayed again. R. Zeira asked, “Why does the Master do so?”: Berakhot 30b. In Gittin 39b, R. Zeira said to R. Chiyya bar Abba, “Did you hear it explicitly or by inference? And has the Master not heard ...?” Berakhot 22a, near the end: R. Chiyya bar Abba said to R. Zeira, “Why does the Master need ...?” And R. Zeira; see Rav Bivi. Zeira questioned him. In the name of R. Chiyya bar Yosef. Chalfa is called his student. R. Chama bar Chanina heard from his lecture. R. Chama bar Yosef—this requires investigation. R. Chanina, his teacher: so Yuchasin writes, but I do not know its basis. R. Chanina of Sura on the Euphrates, his student: so Yuchasin writes, but I do not know its basis. And R. Chanina bar Yosef. R. Chanina bar Agol questioned him. Rabbi Chananyah would lean on him. R. Yehudah bar Nachmani; see above. R. Yehudah Nesia; see above. R. Yehoshua son of R. Nechemyah, in his name. “R. Yehoshua ben Korcha said.” He said to R. Yehoshua ben Levi: Kiddushin 30a; Chullin 98a. R. Yochanan, his teacher. In R. Yochanan's name: Berakhot 14b, 54b, several statements; Shabbat 45a. There, 86b: “R. Chiyya son of Rabbi Abba said: R. Yochanan said.” There, 105b, two statements. Yoma 38b, several statements. Menachot 50b, 74a; Megillah 19b, several statements. Zevachim 25b has “R. Chiyya said: R. Yochanan said”; I think it should read “R. Chiyya bar Abba said,” as the passage indicates. Shabbat 113a has “R. Abba said: R. Chiyya said: R. Yochanan said.” Rif reads “R. Abba said: R. Chiyya bar Abba said: Rav said”; Asheri reads “R. Abba said: R. Chiyya bar Ashi said: Rav said.” In Jerusalem Megillah, chapter 3, halakhah 2, and HaMaddir, halakhah 7, “R. Chiyya said: R. Yochanan said” should, I think, read “R. Chiyya bar Abba said: R. Yochanan said.” R. Yochanan told him, “While you were eating kafniyot in Babylonia ...” Tosafot explains: inferior dates. Responsa Chavvot Yair, section 152, explains this according to R. Ovadiah of Bertinoro at the end of chapter 1 of Orlah, concerning kafniyot still at the blossom stage: Babylonia is low-lying and certainly has good dates, as in Bikkurim, chapter 1; but one ought to wait until they finish ripening, and if one eats them hastily, they are inferior. Likewise, “You have not reached the end of the Mishnah.” Thus in both places he says, “We explained it from its concluding clause”; see there. Bekhorot 18a; Bava Batra 107b. R. Yochanan called him “Babylonian”: Shabbat 105b and Jerusalem Talmud, beginning of Keitzad Mevarkhin. R. Yochanan expounded and everyone ran to hear. R. Chiyya bar Abba rejoiced that in his lifetime he saw R. Yochanan expounding, to whom he had taught aggadah apart from Proverbs and Ecclesiastes: Jerusalem Talmud, end of chapter 2 of Bava Metzia. This is a scribal error; see R. Chananyah above. At the end of Jerusalem Maaserot, R. Yochanan said to him, “Babylonian, from the time I uncovered a potsherd for you, you found a pearl.” In Ketubot, HaKotev, halakhah 11, R. Yochanan told him, “Babylonian, from when I uncovered a potsherd for you—from a pearl” [the source's elliptical wording]. “R. Chiyya bar Abba said: R. Yochanan raised a difficulty in it.” R. Abba said to him, “Perhaps, etc.” They laughed at him: Menachot 74a. R. Yonah, in his name. “R. Yonatan said”—Sanhedrin 7b; Bekhorot 55a. He entrusted words to R. Chiyya bar Abba: Gittin 37a. Rashi apparently regards him as his colleague. R. Chiyya bar Abba and R. Yosi disagree: Shabbat 32b. Which R. Yosi is this? It requires investigation; I think it should read Assi. R. Yannai, his brother. R. Yaakov bar Acha, in his name. And R. Yitzchak Nappacha. And R. Yitzchak ben Elazar. R. Yirmeyah, in his name. Rav Kohen, his brother—this requires investigation. Rav Kahana's life was prolonged through his prayer. Levi bar Chayta, in his name. R. Mana bar Tanchum. Bar Mariya, before him. R. Nachumi, or Nechemyah, his son. R. Nachum, in his name. “R. Chiyya bar Abba said, etc.; R. Nachman said: well done”—Eruvin 32b. Rav Natan Kohen, his brother. Silani asked him. “R. Simai said.” In Ulla's name—Chagigah 25b. R. Pedat, his student. R. Pinchas. “Rav said”—Gittin 38b. And Rava bar Natan. Rava said to him, “Does the Master not hold ...?”: Berakhot 15a; this requires investigation. Rava son of Shmuel, in his name, several statements. Ravin, in his name. Ravnai, or Banah, his brother. R. Shmuel bar Yitzchak asked him and called him “my teacher.” “R. Simlai said.” Rav Shemen bar Abba, the priest—perhaps his brother. Resh Lakish; see above. And R. Shimon bar Abba. Shimon Kamteraya asked him. With R. Tanchum bar Yehudah. R. Tanchum, his son. R. Tanchuma, in his name.
